display.purpose: The page's action-title sentence, max 44ch; 1.5rem under 720px.

figure.purpose: Figure-band values; condensed, tabular, units at 0.55em.

rank.purpose: Memo entry rank numeral; Board variant 1.5rem / 300 / wdth 80; rust for rank 1.

label.purpose: Field labels, memo terms, segmented options.

source.purpose: Source and Note lines under every exhibit.

caption.purpose: Figure subs, hints, marks, table headers, legends.

rules.name: board-rule
rules.purpose: Heads the Board and table header rules.

rules.name: hairline-soft
rules.purpose: Rows inside lists: table rows, evidence items, Board rows.

shadows.name: pop
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: chart tooltip, workspace menu, Ask popover, toast, mobile drawer.

shadows.name: indicator-lift
shadows.purpose: Sliding nav highlight (0.06) and segmented thumb (0.08) only.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default curve for transitions, entrances, draw-ins and bar morphs.

motion.name: page-entry
motion.purpose: Page content on route or workspace change; off when reduced.

motion.name: draw-in-once
motion.value: scaleX or length from baseline, 550-800ms ease-out, stagger capped at 0.3s; in-view once with -40px bottom margin
motion.purpose: Charts, criterion bars and contribution bars the first time they are seen.

motion.name: draw-in-fallback
motion.purpose: If an exhibit has not entered view by 1.2s it renders at rest instantly; no exhibit is ever empty.

motion.name: board-flip
motion.purpose: Opportunity Board re-rank when weights move.

motion.name: board-rank-roll
motion.value: y +/-12px with fade, 220ms ease-out (fade only when reduced)
motion.purpose: Rank numeral change in direction of travel.

motion.name: board-move-count
motion.purpose: Up/down move indicator (verified up, rust down).

motion.name: motion-setting
motion.value: Full | Less | Auto (localStorage fn-motion; Auto follows prefers-reduced-motion)
motion.purpose: Less or a reduce preference sets MotionConfig reducedMotion=always and zeroes JS durations; CSS animations clamp to 1ms under prefers-reduced-motion.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: Score panel moves under finding body; weights grid 2 columns.

breakpoints.name: tablet

narrative.overview:
Every panel in FieldNote is a numbered Exhibit in a consulting deck: a 2px navy rule across the top, a run-in "Exhibit n" set in condensed bold, an action-title sentence that states the conclusion, the figure or chart, and a Source line beneath a hairline. Trust is the grammar of the page. The reader scans titles, checks sources, and drills into evidence without leaving the page.

The material is paper and ink. A white ground (dark mode: deep blue-black paper), navy ink for text, rules and primary actions, steel blue for secondary series and links, and one rust accent kept for the highlighted series, the top rank and the active marker. Structure comes from rules, not boxes: hairlines separate, the 2px exhibit rule opens, and in-flow surfaces carry no shadow. Corners are nearly square (2px). One variable family, Archivo, does all the work. Its width axis tightens numerals and headings, and tabular figures keep columns aligned. Superscript footnote markers tie numbers to their Source lines.

Density is operational: built for a laptop morning scan, with generous exhibit spacing (52px) and tight controls (28 to 36px). Motion is quick and informative, never decorative. Charts draw in once from their baseline, the Board re-ranks with FLIP, and indicators slide between states. Routine transitions stay in the 120 to 320ms band.
keyCharacteristics: Numbered Exhibits with a run-in number, an action title and a Source line
Rules instead of cards: a 2px navy exhibit rule, 1px hairlines, no shadows on in-flow surfaces
One rust accent, reserved for the highlight
Five reserved status markings: verified, thin evidence, disputed, stale, fixture
Archivo Variable with the width axis and tabular lining figures
Fast, ease-out motion that draws in once, with a user Motion setting over prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The One Rust Rule
rules.body: Rust marks the single thing the reader should see first: the highlighted series, rank 1, the active marker. If two things on a screen are rust, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Reserved Status Rule
rules.body: Verified, thin, disputed, stale and fixture hues mean only those states. Never use them for decoration, category or branding.

rules.name: The Stable Entity Rule
rules.body: Entity colour comes from config order through the `c1` to `c8` slots and stays the same on every chart, legend and filter on every page.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can sit next to another number (figures, scores, tables, ranks, marks, chart text) uses `tabular-nums lining-nums`.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Emphasis on numbers and headings comes from narrowing the width axis (78 to 94), not from switching families or adding colour.

rules.name: The Footnote Rule
rules.body: A figure that has a source carries a superscript steel marker (0.68em, weight 700) that matches its numbered Source line.

rules.name: The Rules-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: Group content with a rule above it, never by boxing it in a shadowed card. If a panel needs separation, give it a hairline or a `paper-2` ground.

dos: Do put every panel in a numbered Exhibit with a run-in "Exhibit n", an action-title sentence that states the conclusion, and a Source line.
Do separate with a 2px `rule-strong` exhibit rule and 1px hairlines, and keep in-flow surfaces flat.
Do keep corners at 2px, with 1px for nested indicators.
Do set every comparable number in tabular lining figures, and narrow numerals and headings with the width axis.
Do tie sourced figures to their Source line with a superscript steel footnote marker.
Do assign entity colours from `c1` to `c8` by config order, and fall back to `context`.
Do keep transitions between 120 and 320ms on the ease-out curve, draw charts in once, and honour the Motion setting and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do label fixture data with the hatched fixture band and fixture marks on every page it appears.
donts: Don't build KPI-card grids or coloured cards. Use the figure band and ruled lists instead.
Don't put shadows on in-flow surfaces. Pop is for floating layers only.
Don't use rust for more than one highlight per view, or as a surface or button fill.
Don't use verified, thin, disputed, stale or fixture hues for anything but those states.
Don't introduce a second typeface for display. Archivo's width axis is the display voice.
Don't replay chart draw-ins on re-render, or leave an exhibit empty while it waits for scroll.
